turns.response_html:
I see you have shared a diagram (image_8f3701.png) illustrating a continuous, cyclical workflow between three distinct roles.

Here is a breakdown of the process depicted in your diagram:

1. Research & Planning (Blue)

  • Role: Researcher
  • Activities: The researcher conducts an Interview and defines the Ontology.
  • Outputs: This phase generates a Spec and an Ontologic Plan, which are passed down to the next phase.

2. Strategy & Roadmap (Orange)

  • Role: Manager
  • Activities: Using the specifications provided by the researcher, the manager is responsible for Roadmap Generation.
  • Outputs: This phase produces a tangible Roadmap to guide the workers.

3. Execution & Feedback (Green)

  • Role: Worker
  • Activities: The worker handles the Implementation of the roadmap.
  • Outputs (Feedback Loop): Following implementation, feedback flows back to the Researcher in the form of a Retro-Project and Retro-Tooling, completing the cycle.

What specific aspect of this workflow would you like to explore, document, or modify?

I see you've expanded the workflow in image_8f1d70.png by introducing an external evaluation loop to your system.

Here is a breakdown of the new components and pathways added to the architecture:

New System Components

  • The User Node (Red): You have introduced a fourth role to the cycle, the User, whose primary metric is Satisfaction.
  • External Delivery (Green to Red): The execution phase no longer just loops internally; the Worker's implementation now results in a tangible Product that is delivered directly to the User.
  • Satisfaction Feedback Loop (Red to Blue): Based on their interaction with the Product, the User evaluates their Satisfaction and passes a Grade back up to the Researcher.

The Updated Cycle

This creates a dual-feedback mechanism for the Researcher. They now receive:

  1. Internal Feedback: Retro-Project and Retro-Tooling from the Worker regarding the development experience and system friction.
  2. External Feedback: A Grade from the User regarding the actual viability and success of the output.

How would you like to define the metrics for the "Grade" evaluation, or is there another part of this multi-agent architecture you want to flesh out next?
